t: A Dorian city-state of the Eurotas valley that conquered Messenia and lived off the labour of state-owned serfs, the helots.
With two kings, five ephors and a citizen army trained from childhood, it was the leading land power of Classical Greece.
Sparta led Greece against Persia, defeated Athens in 404 BCE, and lost its power for good at Leuctra in 371 BCE.
dyk: Classical Sparta had no city walls; for centuries it relied on its army alone and was fortified only in the Hellenistic period.
ev: First Messenian War: Sparta conquers Messenia and reduces its people to helots
Leonidas I and 300 Spartiates fall at the Battle of Thermopylae
The regent Pausanias leads the Greeks to victory at the Battle of Plataea
An earthquake strikes Sparta and the helots of Messenia revolt
Athens surrenders to Sparta, ending the Peloponnesian War
Thebes defeats Sparta at the Battle of Leuctra
Cleomenes III is defeated at the Battle of Sellasia
After the Achaean War Sparta becomes a free city allied to Rome
